clue.text: Tisane spiced up a little bit for the discriminating type

indicators.note: spicing something up changes and enlivens it, so the letters of the herbal tea are rearranged

parts.note: a mite is a tiny amount, as in 'a mite cold'

explanation.surface: A herbal tea is given a touch more flavour to suit a fussy drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spiced up' rearranges TISANE into ANTISE. 'Discriminating' suggests a connoisseur with refined taste, but here it means someone who discriminates against a people.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-style description: a person prejudiced against Jews practises discrimination, so is a type who discriminates.

clue.text: Real writer from Germany, not Britain

indicators.note: not tells you the letters for Britain are absent from the writer's name

parts.note: Bertolt Brecht was a German playwright and poet
BR is an abbreviation for Britain or British

explanation.surface: A genuine author who comes from Germany rather than from Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes BR from the playwright's name. The result is itself a German word adopted into English, which the surface quietly hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a German loanword used in English to mean genuine or authentic.

clue.text: It's shaken, not stirred, with unopened Drambuie

indicators.note: stirring mixes things round, so the letters beside it are rearranged
unopened means the word is taken without its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cocktail made the James Bond way, using a sealed bottle of Scotch liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' drops the D of Drambuie, and 'stirred' rearranges NOT with RAMBUIE. The Bond catchphrase hides that 'not' is fodder and 'stirred' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Description by use: a small hand drum with jingles is played by rattling it in the hand.

clue.text: Sharpness that's even in Heidegger?

indicators.note: even points to the letters in the even positions of the philosopher's name, the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: A keenness of mind that is found steadily throughout the philosopher Heidegger's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a blade's keenness, or a keen quality in a voice or performance.

clue.text: Groom wise, so to speak, to conceal conversation with the Parisian adulteress

parts.note: a stable lad is a groom who looks after horses

indicators.note: to conceal means the two letters heard go around the pieces that follow, hiding them inside
so to speak asks you to say the word and listen: it is heard as the plural of a letter's name

parts.note: wise said out loud is 'Ys', that is, two letter Ys
chatter is idle conversation
le is 'the' in French, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A bridegroom is sensible enough to hide his chats with a French woman who is cheating on her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The groom is a stable hand, not a bridegroom. 'so to speak' makes 'wise' the plural of a letter's name, and 'to conceal' wraps that pair round the rest. The answer is D H Lawrence's heroine, who has an affair with her husband's gamekeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the title character of D H Lawrence's novel, a married woman who takes the gamekeeper as her lover.

clue.text: Number passing through island thoroughfare's decreased?

parts.note: I is the map abbreviation for island

indicators.note: something passing through goes inside, so the number sits within the letters for island and thoroughfare

parts.note: Rd is the abbreviation for road, a thoroughfare
one is a number

explanation.surface: The count of vehicles using the main route across an island has gone down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing through' is the insertion signal. The question mark flags the pun: 'decreased' is read as de-creased, with the creases taken out, rather than as a fall in traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Punning sense: clothes that have been pressed have had their wrinkles removed.

clue.text: Appropriate place with Yorkshiremen dropping rugby goal

indicators.note: dropping means the letter for the goal falls away from the town's name

parts.note: Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire, England
rugby goalposts are shaped like a capital H

explanation.surface: A fitting result for a Yorkshire rugby side that lets a drop goal slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes the H off the Yorkshire spa town. 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective meaning suitable; it is the verb, to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to seize or claim something without the right to it.

clue.text: Compiler had turned pale in bar

indicators.note: turned means the two letters for 'compiler had' are written back to front

parts.note: the compiler speaking of themselves says 'I had', shortened to I'd
sallow describes a pale, yellowish complexion

explanation.surface: The crossword setter went white in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' writes ID backwards as DI. The pub is a blind: 'bar' is a verb meaning to forbid.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to refuse to permit or to rule out.

clue.text: Likely lad funny at first

indicators.note: at first says the word for funny goes at the front, ahead of the word for lad

parts.note: funny in the sense of strange is odd
a son is a boy, and 'son' is a way of addressing a lad

explanation.surface: A boy with promise who was amusing to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' only fixes the order of the two halves. The surface nods to The Likely Lads, a British television sitcom, which makes 'Likely lad' look like one unit when the first word alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting term: describes an outcome rated better than evens, so more probable than not.

clue.text: Group of devoted women in wedlock almost wholly defying expectations

indicators.note: in places the group of women inside the word for wedlock

parts.note: a marriage is a union
a convent is a community of nuns, women devoted to religion

indicators.note: almost means the word for wholly loses its last letter

parts.note: all can mean wholly, as in 'all alone'

explanation.surface: A set of dedicated wives who, in their marriages, very nearly completely surprise everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the insertion signal and 'almost' shortens the word for wholly by a letter. The devoted women look like wives, but their devotion is religious: they are nuns.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: not following what is normally done, so surprising people.

clue.text: Painting on fine metallic sheet

indicators.note: on attaches the painting to the letter for fine, which it follows

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
an oil is a painting done in oil paints

explanation.surface: A picture painted on a thin, delicate sheet of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: metal beaten or rolled very thin, as used in the kitchen.

clue.text: Actor is shot capturing Bond's misdeeds

indicators.note: capturing means the rearranged letters take the word for bond inside them
shot can mean ruined or broken, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tie is a bond, as in family ties

explanation.surface: A film star is filmed recreating the wicked acts of James Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges ACTOR IS into ATROCIS, and 'capturing' puts TIE inside. The capital B suggests 007, but the bond is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: extremely wicked or cruel acts, a much stronger word than the clue's.

clue.text: What drug smuggler may do, a mysterious character

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, as in gun-running
E is the usual abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A shadowy figure and the sort of thing a trafficker gets up to.
explanation.walkthrough: The first five words are read together: a smuggler may 'run E', carrying ecstasy. 'Character' is a written symbol, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet, credited with secret or magical meaning.

clue.text: They aren't bound to be complimentary when welcoming man

parts.note: complimentary means given without charge, free

indicators.note: welcoming means the word for when takes the man inside it

parts.note: as can mean when: 'as I left, it rained'
a gent is a man, short for gentleman

explanation.surface: People who are not obliged to say nice things when greeting a chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' is the insertion signal. 'Bound to be' reads as 'certain to be', but 'bound' alone means tied by contract, and 'when' is a piece of wordplay rather than a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: people, such as sports players, who are out of contract and can sign for anyone.

clue.text: Vocal leaders of repertory theatre like luvvies?

indicators.note: vocal means spoken: the two initial letters are said out loud as letter names
the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the leading letters of repertory and theatre are R and T

explanation.surface: Loud leading figures of a theatre company, behaving just as actors do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vocal' asks you to say the initials R and T as letter names. 'Luvvies' is British slang for actors seen as affected and effusive.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose description: showily or pretentiously artistic, as theatrical types are teased for being.

clue.text: Something beaten, a naughty child wearing topaz ring

indicators.note: wearing means the child has the letters for topaz and ring around it, like clothing

parts.note: topaz is a yellowish-brown colour, as is tan
an imp is a mischievous child
a ring is the round letter O

explanation.surface: A badly behaved youngster in a gemstone ring is given a hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' wraps the colour and the round letter about the child. 'Beaten' suggests punishment for that child; it is what a drummer does to an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a kettledrum, an instrument played by striking it.

clue.text: Politician infiltrates society, revealing the fibber's art?

indicators.note: infiltrates means the politician gets inside the letters for society and revealing

parts.note: telling means revealing, as in a telling remark
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: An MP worms into high society and shows off the skill of a liar.
explanation.definitionFit: Double sense: narrating tales is a craft, and telling stories is also a mild way of saying lying.

clue.text: Waterlogged planet hazy around the outside

parts.note: Mars is the fourth planet from the sun

indicators.note: around the outside picks the first and last letters of the word hazy

explanation.surface: A sodden world that looks misty at its edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: describes boggy ground that is saturated with water.

clue.text: Medicinal extract can treat stifling temperature

parts.note: a can is a tin, the usual British word for a food can

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the word for treat closes around the letter for temperature

parts.note: to treat an illness successfully is to cure it
T is the scientific abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy is able to deal with a suffocating fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stifling' puts T inside CURE. 'Can' reads as 'is able to' but is the metal container.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionary sense: a medicine made by dissolving a drug in alcohol.

clue.text: Smart chap admits cover up in foreign accent

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the assembled letters are read from the bottom upwards
admits means the smart chap's name lets the word for cover inside

parts.note: a smart alec is a know-all, so Alec is the smart chap
a lid is a cover for a pot or box

explanation.surface: A clever fellow confesses to a deception, speaking in an overseas voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' makes ALLIDEC, which 'up' then reads from the bottom. 'Admits cover up' looks like confessing to a deception, and the accent is a written mark, not a way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the hook written under a c in French and Portuguese to soften it.

clue.text: Little help if driving with empty engine in US city twice

parts.note: a tee is the peg that props up the ball for a golfer's drive
NY is New York, and 'twice' says it is used two times

indicators.note: empty means the word engine loses its contents, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: the second use of NY, New York

explanation.surface: There is not much assistance for a motorist whose car has no fuel in either of two American cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' hollows out engine, and 'twice' means New York appears once after the golfing peg and again last of all. The driving is golf, not motoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a childish expression meaning very small indeed.

clue.text: Minister breaks back wheel making return for church-goers

parts.note: to back someone is to second them, as with a motion

indicators.note: breaks means the minister splits the word for wheel open and sits inside

parts.note: a cog is a toothed wheel

explanation.surface: A clergyman damages a rear tyre and so earns something back for his congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' is the insertion signal. 'Back wheel' looks like one thing on a bicycle but splits into a verb meaning to support and a toothed gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian doctrine: the expected reappearance of Christ on earth, which believers await.

clue.text: Turn skiff, finally overwhelmed by more confident person on board

parts.note: to wind a handle is to turn it

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the letter is swamped, sitting inside the word for more confident

parts.note: surer means more certain or confident

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word skiff

explanation.surface: A small boat is swung round and at last swamped by a bolder passenger on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the F of skiff and 'overwhelmed by' puts it inside SURER. 'On board' suggests a ship's passenger; the board is a sailboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: someone who rides a board fitted with a sail across the water.

clue.text: Pro getting trees sorted out?

parts.note: pro means in favour of, that is, for

indicators.note: sorted out means put into a new order, so the letters of trees are rearranged

explanation.surface: A professional who keeps woodland in good order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges TREES into ESTER. The whole clue is also the definition, with 'Pro' read as professional.
explanation.definitionFit: Description of the job: a professional who manages and tends woodland.

clue.text: Cut school? Head in irritation gets running

parts.note: a sect is a school of thought or belief

indicators.note: head in picks the leading letter of the word irritation

parts.note: a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: Play truant? The annoyed headteacher starts sprinting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head in' takes the I of irritation. 'Cut school' reads as skipping lessons, but 'Cut' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb or noun: to divide by slicing, or a slice through something.

clue.text: Outside of Sidmouth, like fliers evoking a writer

indicators.note: outside of picks the first and last letters of the town's name

parts.note: avian means of or like birds, which fly

explanation.surface: Just beyond the Devon seaside town of Sidmouth, bird-like creatures bring an author to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective: in the style of the playwright George Bernard Shaw.

clue.text: Perhaps crawl right into Midlands town

indicators.note: into sends the letter for right inside the town's name

parts.note: Stoke, short for Stoke-on-Trent, is a city in the English Midlands known for its potteries

explanation.surface: Traffic may inch along as you turn right into a town in the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts R inside STOKE. The crawl is the swimming style, not slow traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: front crawl is one of the ways of swimming.

clue.text: Deity lives more than once

indicators.note: more than once means the short word for lives is written two times

parts.note: something that lives exists, or simply is

explanation.surface: A god has several lifetimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an ancient Egyptian goddess, wife of Osiris.
